evals.prompt: Implement cache-aside pattern in Go for item status lookups. On cache miss, fetch from PostgreSQL, populate Redis with TTL=300s, on hit return cached value. Handle Redis connection failures gracefully (return DB data, log warning, never fail the request).
evals.expected_output: func (s *Service) GetItemStatus(ctx context.Context, id string) (string, error) { cached, err := s.redis.Get(ctx, cacheKey(id)).Result(); if err == nil { return cached, nil }; if !errors.Is(err, redis.Nil) { s.logger.Warn('redis error', zap.Error(err)) }; status, err := s.db.GetItemStatus(ctx, id); if err != nil { return '', err }; go func() { s.redis.Set(context.Background(), cacheKey(id), status, 5*time.Minute) }(); return status, nil }. Use pipelined writes for multi-key sets. NEVER block requests on Redis failure.

evals.prompt: Design a Redis Sorted Set for a real-time user leaderboard. ZADD operations with score=value, ZREVRANGEBYSCORE top 10. Implement a Redis Lua script to atomically update score and trim to top 1000. Handle TTL for inactive users.
evals.expected_output: ZADD leaderboard:daily {value} {user_id}. ZREVRANGEBYSCORE leaderboard:daily +inf 0 WITHSCORES LIMIT 0 10 for top 10. Lua script: EVAL 'redis.call("ZADD", KEYS[1], ARGV[1], ARGV[2]) redis.call("ZREMRANGEBYRANK", KEYS[1], 0, -1001) return 1' 1 leaderboard:daily {amount} {user_id}. TTL: EXPIRE on inactive leaderboard keys at midnight. Use atomic Lua for update+trim — never two separate calls.

evals.prompt: Troubleshoot cache stampede during a traffic spike. 1000 concurrent requests hit the same cache key simultaneously. Implement probabilistic early recomputation (XFetch algorithm) and Redis SETNX-based mutex to prevent DB overload.
evals.expected_output: Cache stampede fix: before expiration, use XFetch — at time delta = expiry - beta * log(random()), if delta < 0, recompute early. Mutex lock via SETNX lock:{key} with TTL=10s — only one goroutine recomputes, others serve stale data or wait. Config: beta=1.0, recompute at 80% TTL remaining. NEVER allow all requests to hit DB simultaneously. NEVER use DEL+SET (non-atomic, causes stampede on delete).
